title: Woman dies after being shot by Calgary police officer
article: Calgary police have confirmed a woman who was shot by an officer during an early morning altercation has died.
The Alberta Serious Incident Response Team is investigating.

Police were called to the 2000 block of 35th Street S.E. at about 6 a.m. in response to a report of a suspicious person wandering in and out of backyards in the area. A confrontation occurred between the officer and the woman before she was shot.
The woman, who was carrying pepper spray, discharged it on the uniformed officer who subsequently fired her weapon. Police said the suspect was known to them.
Calgary police Chief Mark Neufeld attended the scene of the shooting, sources indicated.

Cally Berry, who has lived in the area for four years, said she was woken up by officers pounding on her front door. Berry said she looked out to the alley where about a dozen police cruisers were parked.
Berry said she didn't see or hear anything suspicious, but has had her garage and vehicle broken into in the same alley.
"There's been a lot of petty theft, you know, cars being broken into and windshields being smashed," she said.
"Our main concern is that there's this daycare right here," she said, pointing to the Davar Child Development Centre that was partially blocked off by police tape Wednesday morning.
At a news conference Wednesday afternoon, acting Deputy Chief Steve Barlow said the officer involved has received medical attention and psychological services.
"I can only commend her on how she handled the situation," Barlow said. "It's a horrible outcome. . . No officer ever comes to work wanting to be in a situation like this."
The officer involved in the incident, who's been with the service for six years, received medical treatment at the scene, police said.
She's also been placed on a 30-day administrative leave.
